definition: the process green plants use to turn sunlight, water and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen
sentence: Thanks to photosynthesis, the cedar trees release the oxygen Ace breathes on his hike.

definition: the green chemical in plants that captures energy from sunlight
sentence: Leaves look green because they are full of chlorophyll.

definition: a tiny green part inside a plant cell where photosynthesis happens
sentence: Under the microscope, Ace counted dozens of chloroplasts in a single leaf cell.

definition: describing trees that lose all their leaves every autumn
sentence: The deciduous maple in the backyard drops its orange leaves every October.

definition: describing trees that grow cones and usually keep their needles all year
sentence: Most of the trees in BC's coastal rainforest are coniferous, like the Douglas fir.

definition: the moment a seed begins to sprout and grow
sentence: Warm, damp soil helped the germination of Ace's bean seeds.

definition: the loss of water vapour from a plant's leaves into the air
sentence: On hot days, transpiration pulls water all the way up from the roots to the leaves.

definition: a simple sugar that plants make and living things use for energy
sentence: The leaves turn sunlight into glucose, which the tree uses to grow.

definition: the layer of small trees and shrubs that grows beneath a forest's tall canopy (Canadian spelling)
sentence: Ferns and huckleberry bushes fill the shady understorey of the rainforest.

definition: a living thing, such as a fungus or bacterium, that breaks down dead plants and animals
sentence: Fungi are decomposers that slowly turn a fallen log into rich soil.
